name: Tessera TAR-12 'Consensus'
description:
Tessera's flagship assault rifle integrates their proprietary distributed targeting AI, which networks multiple TAR-12 units into a cooperative fire-control system. When a squad carries Consensus rifles, each weapon's BCI link shares targeting data, automatically deconflicting fire lanes and prioritizing threats based on collective sensor input. The result is a squad that shoots with the coordination of a single intelligence.

The TAR-12 fires 5.8mm polymer-tipped rounds from a 35-round box magazine, with a secondary electromagnetic acceleration rail that can be toggled for armor-piercing velocity at the cost of increased power cell drain. The rifle's modular chassis accepts Tessera's ecosystem of smart attachments, from thermal imaging foregrips to predictive recoil compensation stocks.

The Consensus is expensive — a full squad kit runs upward of Φ80,000 — but organizations that field it report 40% improvement in engagement efficiency. Critics call it a crutch that degrades individual marksmanship. Operators call it winning.
legality: Restricted — licensed military and premium security
specifications:
caliber: 5.8mm polymer-tipped
effective_range: 500m (standard), 650m (EM-accelerated)
rate_of_fire: 800 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 35 rounds
weight: 3.8 kg (base)
tactical_use: The TAR-12 transforms squad tactics from individual marksmanship into networked lethality. The distributed AI automatically assigns targets, calls out flanking threats, and coordinates suppressive fire without verbal communication. In urban environments where communication is jammed, the weapon-to-weapon mesh network operates on encrypted short-range protocols that are extremely difficult to intercept.
cultural_context: The Consensus represents Tessera's philosophy that technology should amplify collective human capability rather than replace it. Owning one without the squad network is like owning half a weapon — the rifle functions independently, but its true potential requires the full ecosystem. This has created a dependency model that critics liken to corporate lock-in disguised as tactical superiority.
story_hooks: A hacker has found a way to inject false targeting data into the TAR-12's mesh network, turning a squad's coordinated fire against friendly positions.
A black-market dealer is selling individual TAR-12s stripped of their networking capability — but the distributed AI still phones home to Tessera.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular assault rifle with a distinctly modular architecture. The Consensus has a forward-swept profile with pronounced mounting rails integrated into the upper receiver. Its silhouette reads as purposefully networked — clusters of sensor ports and BCI interface nodes break up the traditional rifle form, giving it an almost distributed, multi-component appearance despite being a unified weapon.
physical_description.dimensions: 965mm overall length, 210mm width at rail cluster, 85mm height at charging handle. Barrel length: 405mm. Modular receiver accepts variable-length tactical packages.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly balanced despite its 3.8kg mass — the distributed smart-attachment interface centers weight around the midline, making it feel nimble in trained hands. The electromagnetic rail assembly in the stock area adds subtle heft toward the rear without feeling nose-heavy.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon-composite chassis with reinforced aluminum alloy upper receiver. Polymer-injected components reduce weight while maintaining structural rigidity. The EM-acceleration rail assembly uses hardened steel internals.
physical_description.finish: Matte graphite-black composite with brushed titanium accent panels along the modular attachment points. The upper receiver features a subtle iridescent coating that shifts faintly blue-to-purple under certain light angles — a Thoughtline signature. Wear surfaces show raw composite texture beneath the matte treatment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant matte black with brushed titanium/silver accents. LED indicator clusters glow soft cyan when networked, shifting to amber when in autonomous mode. Internal rail systems show faint copper-bronze coloring.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with integrated pressure sensors (detectable as micro-texture ridges). The charging handle is wrapped in textured aramid fiber. Magazine well has precision-molded grip ridges for swift magazine changes.
distinctive_features: Integrated BCI neural-link socket mounted above the charging handle — three contact points flush with the receiver
Distributed sensor cluster: three small LiDAR ports along the top rail, two thermal sensing windows in the foregrip mounting
Electromagnetic acceleration rail visible through semi-transparent polymer access panel in stock — faint electrical tracery visible within
Modular attachment rail system with 12-point quick-disconnect nodes across upper and side receivers
Ammo counter display in the magazine housing — small LED window showing round count
Heat venting louvers along the barrel shroud in geometric V-pattern
Thoughtline logo embossed (not stamped) on the left side of upper receiver — subtle, matte-on-matte aesthetic
Encrypted dataport near the trigger guard for weapon firmware updates
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Thoughtline Messaging logo (stylized Φ symbol integrated into a mesh network pattern) embossed on left upper receiver. Serial number laser-etched in microscopic text on the mag well. 'CONSENSUS TAR-12' marked along the barrel in minimalist sans-serif font. Tiny regulatory compliance stamps on the safety selector.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show subtle wear patterns: scuff marks on the composite from gear contact, micro-scoring on the modular rail points from repeated attachment cycles, and slight discoloration around the BCI socket from repeated neural-link coupling. Well-maintained by operators who understand the weapon's complexity — batteries topped, firmware current, sensor windows kept clear.
